interactions.label: Why is aggressive blood pressure reduction avoided in the acute phase of ischaem

params.question: Why is aggressive blood pressure reduction avoided in the acute phase of ischaemic stroke when thrombolysis is not planned?

answers.text: Antihypertensive drugs interact with alteplase and increase haemorrhagic risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The question specifies thrombolysis is NOT planned, so alteplase interaction is irrelevant. When thrombolysis IS planned, blood pressure is lowered to below 185/110 before administration.

answers.text: The ischaemic penumbra depends on maintained perfusion pressure to remain viable

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The ischaemic penumbra — the at-risk tissue surrounding the infarct core — relies on collateral blood flow driven by systemic pressure. Lowering BP reduces perfusion to this vulnerable zone, potentially converting salvageable tissue into permanent infarct.

answers.text: Rapid blood pressure reduction causes rebound intracranial hypertension

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rebound intracranial hypertension is not the mechanism. The concern is inadequate perfusion of the penumbra, not a pressure rebound effect.

answers.text: Cerebral autoregulation is enhanced during acute stroke and compensates automatically

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cerebral autoregulation is actually impaired in acute ischaemic stroke. This impairment is precisely why systemic blood pressure matters — the brain cannot compensate for pressure drops.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. In acute ischaemic stroke, the penumbra relies on systemic blood pressure for perfusion. Aggressive lowering can extend the infarct by starving salvageable tissue of blood flow.
Correct. The ischaemic penumbra depends on adequate perfusion pressure. Permissive hypertension up to 220/120 mmHg protects salvageable brain tissue when thrombolysis is not planned.

interactions.label: A DEXA scan showing a T-score of −2.5 or lower is required before a diagnosis of

params.question: A DEXA scan showing a T-score of −2.5 or lower is required before a diagnosis of osteoporosis can be made in a patient who has fractured after a standing-height fall.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Not quite. A fragility fracture alone is diagnostic of osteoporosis. A DEXA scan quantifies bone density but is not a prerequisite when the fracture mechanism already demonstrates pathological bone weakness. Any fracture from a standing-height fall meets the clinical definition.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A fragility fracture — any fracture from a fall at standing height or less — is clinically diagnostic of osteoporosis regardless of DEXA availability. The low-energy mechanism proves the bone is pathologically weak, meeting the definition without requiring densitometry.

interactions.label: Why is the target oxygen saturation in a COPD exacerbation set at 88–92% rather

params.question: Why is the target oxygen saturation in a COPD exacerbation set at 88–92% rather than the usual 94–98%?

answers.text: Pulse oximeters consistently overestimate saturation in chronic lung disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While oximetry can have limitations, the lower target is not due to measurement error. It is a deliberate therapeutic choice based on respiratory drive physiology in chronic CO₂ retainers.

answers.text: Chronic CO₂ retainers rely on hypoxic drive for respiration; excessive oxygen suppresses this and risks hypercapnic coma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In chronic CO₂ retainers, the normal hypercapnic drive is blunted and respiration depends on hypoxic drive. High-flow oxygen removes this stimulus, causing hypoventilation, CO₂ accumulation, and potentially fatal respiratory acidosis.

answers.text: Higher oxygen concentrations directly worsen bronchospasm and airway inflammation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oxygen does not worsen bronchospasm. The danger is suppression of the hypoxic respiratory drive, not worsening of airway disease.

answers.text: Elderly patients have physiologically lower oxygen requirements that need no correction

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The lower target is specific to COPD patients with chronic CO₂ retention, not a general age-related adjustment. It applies because these patients depend on hypoxia as their breathing stimulus.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. COPD patients with chronic CO₂ retention rely on low oxygen levels to stimulate breathing. Raising SpO₂ above 92% can suppress this hypoxic drive, causing dangerous CO₂ accumulation.

Correct. Chronic CO₂ retainers depend on hypoxic drive for breathing. Over-oxygenation removes that stimulus, leading to hypoventilation and potentially fatal hypercapnic coma — hence the conservative 88–92% target.

interactions.label: A 78-year-old woman on long-term prednisolone for rheumatoid arthritis requires

params.question: A 78-year-old woman on long-term prednisolone for rheumatoid arthritis requires emergency surgery for a hip fracture. What is the correct perioperative corticosteroid management?

answers.text: Taper and discontinue prednisolone 48 hours before surgery to reduce infection risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Abruptly stopping long-term corticosteroids risks adrenal crisis — the suppressed hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis cannot mount an adequate cortisol response to surgical stress, potentially causing cardiovascular collapse.

answers.text: Continue the usual maintenance dose without adjustment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The usual maintenance dose is insufficient for surgical stress. The body normally surges cortisol output several-fold during surgery; a suppressed adrenal axis cannot produce this increase independently.

Patients on long-term corticosteroids have a suppressed HPA axis and cannot generate the cortisol surge needed during surgery. Stress-dose hydrocortisone provides this critical support and prevents adrenal crisis.

answers.text: Replace prednisolone with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug before surgery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: NSAIDs cannot replace corticosteroids here. The issue is adrenal suppression from chronic steroid use, not anti-inflammatory coverage. Moreover, NSAIDs carry serious renal and gastrointestinal risks in elderly surgical patients.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. Long-term corticosteroid use suppresses the adrenal glands. Without stress-dose hydrocortisone, the patient cannot produce the cortisol surge surgery demands, risking cardiovascular collapse from adrenal crisis.

Correct. Chronic steroid use suppresses the HPA axis, so the adrenals cannot mount a stress response. Stress-dose hydrocortisone prevents perioperative adrenal crisis — steroids must never be stopped abruptly before surgery.

interactions.label: A post-stroke patient scores 45 on the Barthel Index. What rehabilitation dispos

params.question: A post-stroke patient scores 45 on the Barthel Index. What rehabilitation disposition does this score indicate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A Barthel score above 60 is needed to predict likely home discharge. At 45, the patient has too much functional dependence for safe discharge directly home.

The Barthel Index scores ten daily activities from 0 to 100. A score between 20 and 60 indicates moderate dependence requiring structured inpatient rehabilitation. The goal is to improve function above 60 — the threshold predicting successful home discharge.
Intensive support is indicated for scores below 20, reflecting severe dependence. A score of 45 indicates moderate dependence amenable to active rehabilitation, not custodial care.

answers.text: Community-based rehabilitation with no inpatient stay required

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Community-based programmes lack the intensity and supervision needed at this level of functional dependence. Inpatient rehabilitation provides the structured, high-intensity practice that drives recovery.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. The Barthel Index has three key bands: above 60 predicts home discharge, 20–60 requires inpatient rehabilitation, and below 20 needs intensive support. A score of 45 falls squarely in the inpatient rehabilitation range.
Correct. A Barthel score of 45 falls in the 20–60 range, indicating moderate dependence requiring inpatient rehabilitation to reach the home-discharge threshold of above 60.
